baseline_definition: The historical standalone evidence baseline measures progress toward four self-contained field units that do not depend on a phone, server, or repeater; it is retained for continuity and is not the current V1 Companion release total.

baseline_milestones.description: Protocol, recovery, privacy, group-size, and degraded-operation rules are documented and extensively host tested. OT-091 freezes the algorithm-neutral secure-LoRa lifecycle/admission semantics without selecting cryptography, implementing packet v1, or adding physical evidence. OT-093 freezes the deterministic candidate-free pre-crypto build baseline. OT-094 freezes the historical six-blocker readiness contract. OT-095 freezes historical source-lock admission semantics, OT-096 records the bounded 5/8 mbedTLS static assessment, OT-097 freezes license-aware OTCSL0/v1, OT-098 records external-source inspection, OT-099 records complete libsodium managed-import evidence plus an isolated generic ESP32-S3 computer-build pass, OT-100 accepts only the exact OT-099 libsodium source lock, OT-102 accepts exact Monocypher 4.0.3 source evidence under the owner-selected BSD-2-Clause branch, and OT-103 admits the exact received OT-DEV-001 profile. Historical six-blocker, prior five-blocker, and prior four-blocker states remain recorded; three current readiness requirements remain. OT-103 adds bounded physical identity evidence only; none of these increments runs a benchmark, selects cryptography, proves support, compatibility, regulatory acceptance, or direct-radio behavior, or adds crypto implementation. OT-105 accepts only the exact pinned ESP-IDF v6.0.2 / mbedTLS 4.1.0 source dependency lock; history is now historical six, prior five, prior four, prior three, and current three requirements, accepted source/API-configuration/import counts are 3/0/0, and readiness remains blocked.

baseline_milestones.name: Heltec V4 bench firmware
baseline_milestones.description: Two assembled Heltec V4 units retain bounded historical MeshCore bench evidence. OT-DEV-001 is an experimental OpenTrail target with exact-profile build, physical boot/BLE advertisement, and startup/status OLED evidence. OT-083 and OT-084 reject both on-chip authorization rollback-floor candidates; Decision 0033 preserves that result for rollback-proof ownership while permitting practical physical-presence authorization under the disclosed physical-reflash limit. OT-090 freezes and host-tests that exact pairing/reconnect/replacement contract without target, Android, storage, pairing, protected-control, or physical evidence, and OT-091 freezes the separate algorithm-neutral secure-LoRa lifecycle/admission semantics without crypto selection, implementation, or physical evidence. OT-093 freezes an exact two-build candidate-free pre-crypto baseline for the unsupported bench target. OT-094 freezes the blocked readiness contract while exact received revision/RF identity, final candidate configuration, dependency locks, and direct-radio region/MTU/PHY remain unresolved. OT-095 freezes source-lock admission semantics while accepting, acquiring, and importing zero sources; none of these increments is an OT-005 benchmark, target-support result, crypto selection, implementation, or physical evidence. OT-085A installed and verified the exact OT-085 image, accepted one fixed privacy-safe public BLE read, and physically observed `BLE CONNECTED` followed by the phone-disconnect return to `BLE ADVERTISING`. OT-085B accepted target-initiated automatic termination inside the bounded interval, the same owner-observed display lifecycle, and return of exactly one compatible service advertiser without claiming stable identity; every protected characteristic, claim, and command remains closed. OT-103 now binds OT-DEV-001 to the exact received Heltec Automation WiFi LoRa 32 V4 / HTIT-WB32LAF / V4.2 documented-high-band profile using owner-provided photos and official documentation. That bounded identity closes only the exact-profile requirement; it does not prove support, compatibility, antenna suitability, radio behavior, legal-region configuration, regulatory acceptance, or benchmark readiness. OT-106 separately promotes the accepted compact footer into the production UI component and proves deterministic build linkage in two fresh pinned computer-only builds. The target still binds no live battery, GNSS, or LoRa-activity source, so the footer remains at fail-closed placeholders with a blank direction field; no device, flash, radio, physical-display, live-telemetry, support, readiness, final-configuration, crypto, regulatory, or score claim is added. All five OT-093 files remain unchanged: its frozen mixed-EOL `3837dbce...` digest is immutable but non-reconstructible, while the distinct deterministic `c84ba0e3...` checkout aggregate neither replaces nor reconstructs it. The exact installed partition/source proof, private OT-064 recovery application, recovery contracts, and dormant protected-root foundations remain accepted historical evidence without current runtime authority.
baseline_milestones.evidence_status: Experimental physical target with bounded public BLE link
baseline_milestones.next_gate: Close the three current OTCBR0 readiness requirements, accept a new immutable executable benchmark plan, run the exact comparison under separate authority, and explicitly accept the suite/wire selection; then implement the frozen OT-090 and OT-091 contracts under separate target/app/radio authority.
